newsitem.title: LATVIA: DEPOSITORY SATISFIED WITH ESTONIAN AGREEMENT.
newsitem.headline: DEPOSITORY SATISFIED WITH ESTONIAN AGREEMENT.

text.p: The Latvian central depository (LCD) said on Thursday that it was satisfied with the initial results produced by an agreement with its Estonian counterpart allowing brokerages to open cross-border securities accounts.

The LCD has registered Estonian securities worth 1.64 million lats while accounts in the Estonian depository contain Latvian securities worth 13,000 lats, LCD president Martinsh Rikshis said at a news conference.
"I am glad that...Estonian securities are flowing into Latvia," Rikshis said.
He added that earlier concerns that Estonian investors would dominate under the deal have not come true.
"The tendencies are positive and I expect the process to continue," Rikshis said.
Rikshis also said that Uhispank and Unibanka, the second biggest banks in Estonia and Latvia respectively, have attracted most of the investor interest.
The Estonian depository, with a market cap of $1.51 billion, $1.23 billion in shares, has nine account holders, all of them banks, Rikshis said.
"This makes us realize how many account holders can perform viably on the much smaller Latvian market," Rikshis said, referring to the 23 account holders, four of them brokerages, with the LCD.
The market cap of securities registered in the LCD as of July 1 was $595 million, $302 million in shares.
"Latvia should in the nearest future allow brokerages to apply for a license allowing them to conduct securities transactions without being an account holder," Rikshis said.
